title: Fairshare metering & stream-credit pilot for Hosted API
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Summary: Pilot a 'fairshare' metering model for the Hosted API that treats input (ingress) and output (egress) tokens as distinct billable streams with an additive credit system for streaming sessions. The core idea is to reduce friction for streaming-first workloads (e.g., chat UI + real-time assistants) by offering small per-session warm-start credits and a bidirectional ledger that prevents double-charging while keeping unit economics transparent for downstream enterprise contracts and security questionnaire responses.

Goals:
- Measure customer behavior change and retention for streaming-heavy apps when offered session credits + distinct ingress/egress rates.
- Quantify revenue and margin impact vs current unified per-token pricing.
- Validate billing clarity in enterprise SQ responses and contract templates (legal).
- Ensure no regressions in latency or platform load from added billing telemetry.

Hypotheses:
H1: Providing a 25-token warm-start credit per active stream session will increase streaming session frequency by at least 12% for target cohort.
H2: Separating ingress/egress unit prices (input cheaper than output) will discourage needless assistant-token inflation and reduce average output token per request by ~8%.
H3: Clear per-direction billing will reduce enterprise SQ follow-ups related to 'token accounting' by >50%.

Experiment design:
- Cohorts: control (current unified per-token model) vs variant A (distinct IO rates, no session credits) vs variant B (distinct IO rates + 25-token session credit). Randomized assignment per customer org with stratification by monthly spend bucket and vertical.
- Billing: Instrumented metering that emits per-request records with fields: org_id, request_id, model, seq_len_in, seq_len_out, streaming_session_id (when present). Aggregation layer computes daily ingress/egress totals and applies session credit reconciliation.
- Duration: 8 weeks (2-week ramp, 4-week steady-state, 2-week cool-down).
- Sample size: target 200 active orgs per cohort (power calc attached in doc link).

Success metrics:
- Primary: net revenue delta per MAU, churn rate over experiment window, and session frequency uplift.
- Secondary: average tokens per response (output), number of enterprise SQ clarifications, billing-related support tickets.
- Safety: no >5% increase in median 95th-percentile latency across api routes; billing pipeline error rate <0.1%.

Telemetry & instrumentation:
- New BigQuery tables: hosted_billing.ingress_egress_v2 (schema stable), streaming.sessions_credit_log.
- Dashboards: pricing-experiments/fairshare-pilot (key charts: revenue delta, token distribution by direction, session frequency, billing error rate).
- Alerts: billing reconciliation lag > 1h, credit application failure rate >0.01%.

Rollout plan:
Phase 0 (Week -1 to 0): finalize legal/finance accounting treatment and update contract language for enterprise pilots.
Phase 1 (Week 1-2): small canary to 10 low-risk orgs, verify telemetry and reconciliation.
Phase 2 (Week 3-6): ramp to full cohort assignment.
Phase 3 (Week 7-8): analyze results, executive review, and decision to promote/abort.

Dependencies:
- Eng: metering schema change and reconciliation job (ENG-48210).
- Infra: dashboards, alerting, query cost budget (ENG-47902).
- Legal/Finance: updated T&Cs and enterprise contract addendum wording.

Risks & mitigations:
- Complexity in reconciling session credits across multi-region sessions: mitigate by scoping initial pilot to a single region (us-west-2).
- Customer confusion: include explicit billing preview UI in console for pilot participants and customer-facing FAQ.
- Gaming of credits: limit credits to 1 per active connection per minute and log anomalies for review.

Deliverables:
- Experiment spec and power calc doc (linked).
- Instrumentation PRs and migration plan.
- Finance P&L sensitivity analysis for 12/24 month horizon.
- Post-mortem with recommendations and suggested contract language for enterprise customers.

Note: This pilot is intended to feed both hosted pricing evolution and enterprise contract language (SQ) so Legal will be looped for all pilot communications.
